newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:

* On Monday, the Dow Jones industrial average jumped 76.58 points, a gain of 1.10 percent, to 7,008.20, boosted by big gains in International Business Machines Corp. and Philip Morris Cos. Inc., but bonds and the dollar fell.

* Director General of Taxation Fuad Bawazier has been reported as saying his office would process value added tax refunds for export oriented firms within 10 days of exporters filing their tax refund invoices.
* On Monday, the Jakarta Composite Index eased 0.47 points, or 0.07 percent, to close at 696.03 points as big-capitalised stocks fell.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,392.00/3.00 in early trading against the opening of 2,392.00/2.50.
* Conglomerate Bimantara Citra on a report that it would start the operating a car assembly plant with South Korea's Hyundai Motor Company next year in West Java.
* Car maker Astra International on a media report last Friday that the company and its Japanese principal had discussed the national car program and increasing local content in their products.
* Holding company Bakrie & Brothers on reports that the group was planning to set up consortium with several local businessmen to buy the private-owned Bank Pacific.

* Cement maker Indocement of the Salim group which also operates the biggest flour producer in Indonesia through its unit PT Bogasari Flour Mills, after a report that the firm welcomed the entry of new players into the flour market.
* Chemical producer PT Try Polyta on reports it posted a 10.6 billion rupiah net loss in fourth quarter of last year after on a net income of 8.3 billion rupiah in the same period of 1995.

* Retailer Multipolar and Hero Supermarket on intense speculation that Lippo Group had been targeted Hero for a take-over or link-up despite company denials. Also on recent reports saying that the founder of retailer Matahari, Hari Darmawan, was planning to take a stake in the firm after Multipolar recently took a 50.1 controlling interest in Matahari.
* Shoe maker Ganda Wangsa Utama on market speculation that the company might attract new investors, have a stock split or issue bonus shares.
* Bank Bira on a report that a foreign financial magazine has given the bank its award for the best domestic investment bank in Asia Pacific.
